title: CT CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST
author: Grace Lindqvist, MD
impression:
1. Moderate centrilobular emphysema.
2. 7 mm solid right upper lobe pulmonary nodule in a high-risk patient. Recommend CT chest in 6-12 months (Fleischner Society 2017), then consider CT at 18-24 months.
3. Mild coronary artery calcification.
notes: Exam done without contrast; the report notes an iodinated contrast allergy.

sections.heading: Clinical history
sections.text: COPD, former smoker (40 pack-years, quit 2021). Worsening dyspnea.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.text: Axial CT images of the chest without intravenous contrast. Low-dose protocol. Coronal and sagittal reformats.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text:
Lungs: Moderate centrilobular and paraseptal emphysema, upper lobe predominant. 7 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe (series 3, image 48). No consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
Airways: Mild bronchial wall thickening.
Mediastinum: No lymphadenopathy by size criteria. Heart size normal. Mild coronary artery calcification.
Upper abdomen: Unremarkable.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text:
1. Moderate centrilobular emphysema.
2. 7 mm solid right upper lobe pulmonary nodule in a high-risk patient. Recommend CT chest in 6-12 months (Fleischner Society 2017), then consider CT at 18-24 months.
3. Mild coronary artery calcification.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.text: Non-contrast CT chest in 6-12 months for the right upper lobe nodule.

diagnoses.text: 7 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe (series 3, image 48).

follow_ups.text: Non-contrast CT chest in 6-12 months for the right upper lobe nodule.
